question: Freeze OM baseline expressive-media model: first-class stickers plus generic looping animation/GIF experience, safe canonical media kinds/formats/transcoding, reactions/custom emoji relationship and offline behavior.
provisional_direction: Yes to stickers and GIF-like animated media as expected messenger basics; protocol should model an Animation media kind rather than depend on the legacy GIF codec.
resolution: Resolved: semantic expressive kinds use bounded inert WebP baseline profiles; sent media is immutable BlobID-addressed and pack/catalog independent.

question: Design portable external StickerPack/ContentPack manifests, creator signing/provenance, direct install/share/import/export, emoji/keyword indexing, pack updates/forks, safe static/animated/video formats, licensing metadata and resource limits without an OM-operated mandatory catalog.
provisional_direction: Learn from Telegram: open creation, packs installable from any sticker/message/link, emoji shortcuts, static/animated/video artwork, easy resharing; keep packs independently hostable.
resolution: Resolved: portable data-only ContentPackID with immutable canonical releases, optional signed update lineage, provenance/licensing metadata, direct install/mirroring and explicit fork semantics; no mandatory catalog.

question: Decide whether OM defines only a generic optional entitlement/commerce extension for paid creator packs, while payment rails/marketplaces remain external operator plugins, or whether even entitlement semantics should wait.
provisional_direction: Do not put payment processing, cryptocurrency/token settlement or marketplace operation in OM Core. Preserve a later interoperable entitlement hook so artists/providers can sell without making SeedLife merchant/payment operator.
resolution: Resolved: optional generic EntitlementPresentation may gate pack acquisition/update; OM Core defines no payment/settlement/pricing/tax/refund/marketplace operation and entitlements never gate rendering of already-delivered chat content.

question: Freeze bot/LLM/agent principal and capability model: installation, commands, scopes, selected-context disclosure, streaming responses, local versus remote agents, bot-to-bot behavior, automation and revocation.
provisional_direction: LLMs are explicit service principals/bots, never ambient readers. Prefer scoped invocation/selected context; full-room membership is visibly a plaintext recipient.
resolution: Resolved: typed ServicePrincipal/ServiceID with separately authorized endpoints; selected-context is default, scoped subscription/full-Room membership are explicit, local/remote LLM and tool/network capabilities are separated, automation is bounded/revocable.

question: Define the composable social hierarchy for private groups, Spaces/Communities and independent Rooms/Channels, including membership inheritance versus independent membership, shared style/policy and room linking.
provisional_direction: Synthesize Matrix Spaces (container of independent rooms), Discord server/channel organization, Telegram 2026 Communities (linked groups/channels/bots) and WhatsApp-style simple announcements; avoid a mandatory homeserver.
resolution: Resolved: Space/Community is a provider-independent organizational/control container linking independent Rooms/Publications/nested Spaces. Space membership does not auto-join Rooms; official links are bilateral; Room authority-parent delegation is explicit and room-localized.

question: Define broadcast/publication room semantics distinct from private MLS group chat: private subscriber broadcast, public signed publication, replies/discussion linking, subscriber privacy, discovery and provider responsibilities.
provisional_direction: Support broadcast channels, but keep public publication/discovery as separate optional capabilities/operators rather than quietly turning private chat into a social network.
resolution: Resolved: private announcements are permission-restricted MLS Rooms; public one-to-many feeds are separate signed Publications with non-canonical subscriber lists and optional independent discussion Rooms; V1 adds no massive-private-broadcast cryptosystem.

question: Design scoped roles/permissions/rules for Communities/Spaces and Rooms: inheritance/overrides, admin delegation, moderation actions, bot permissions, quorum for high-risk changes and constitutional fork behavior.
provisional_direction: Learn from Discord role/channel permissions but avoid one unrestricted Administrator super-role as an architectural necessity; authority should remain capability-scoped.
resolution: Resolved: capabilities are authority; roles are named grant bundles; explicit restrictions subtract authority; delegation ceilings prevent self-escalation; no permanent owner or unrestricted Administrator bypass is required; high-risk changes may require quorum.

question: Choose the conversation-organization model: lightweight reply threads, persistent forum topics, Zulip-style topic labels, or a layered combination that stays simple for small groups and powerful for large ones.
provisional_direction: Use ordinary chat by default; add persistent topic/forum capability for busy rooms. Study Zulip topic navigation and Discord/Telegram forums rather than forcing topics on every conversation.
resolution: Resolved: layered reply -> lightweight same-Room thread -> persistent room-local Topic. Topics have no separate membership/MLS state; chat is default and forum mode may require topics.

question: Freeze the plugin/app extension security model that lets OneMessenger gain optional capabilities without fragmenting core compatibility: client plugins, protocol extensions, bots, provider plugins, UI surfaces, permissions, signing and sandboxing.
provisional_direction: Extensions must be explicit, scoped, sandboxed/data-only where possible, independently implementable and criticality-negotiated; absence of an optional plugin must not break baseline OM.
resolution: Resolved: protocol/data/local-Wasm/web-service/provider extension classes are distinct; official-client executable plugins use capability-scoped WebAssembly Component Model/WIT with no ambient authority; shared canonical semantics require published protocol schemas.

question: Define the first-release messenger feature baseline needed for traction (reply/quote, reactions, edit/delete policy, voice notes, files/media, camera, GIF/stickers, mentions, polls, pins, search, mute/archive, typing/presence/receipts, calls, groups, contact sharing, block/report) and mark each as core, extension or later.
provisional_direction: Ship a familiar messenger before exotic ecosystem features; basic expressive and group ergonomics are adoption requirements, not optional polish.
resolution: Resolved in MESSENGER_BASELINE_V1.md: ordinary messenger product baseline and each shared/local/optional/later semantic boundary are explicit, including pins, polls, forwarding, voice notes, scheduling, calls and moderation redaction.

question: Define OpenMessenger interconnection boundaries for independent clients and external-network bridges: principal identity, capability discovery, plaintext trust boundary, room mapping, loops, edits/deletes/reactions fidelity and security-state UI.
provisional_direction: Independent OM clients are first-class. External-network bridges are explicit gateway principals; E2EE ends where a bridge decrypts, and the UI must never hide that boundary.
resolution: Resolved: typed BridgePrincipal with bridge-attested foreign provenance; explicit private-Room plaintext/E2EE boundary; capability/fidelity mapping, loop lineage, and evidence-only foreign identity links.

question: Freeze user-owned import/export/escape semantics: portable export of OM identity-independent user state/history where safe, provider/client migration, provenance, selective export, and adapter boundaries for importing data from other messengers without making OM a data trap.
provisional_direction: Own/OpenMessenger requires a documented escape hatch. Export should use documented portable formats and preserve provenance/security limitations; migration must not require SeedLife or one client vendor.
resolution: Resolved: public om-archive-v1 portability model preserves exact native evidence where available, separates history from authority, treats foreign imports as non-routable ImportedHistoryRecords, and requires provider/client escape without SeedLife.

question: Run a dedicated adversarial metadata pass across relays/providers/Spaces/Rooms/Publications/bots/push/attachments/migrations: timing, traffic volume, group size/membership, child-link visibility, contact relationships, attachment sizes, push activity, role changes and cross-provider correlation.
provisional_direction: Do not claim metadata privacy from content E2EE alone. Minimize stable correlators, make exposure provider-capability-visible, and distinguish UI hiding from cryptographic/selective-disclosure privacy.
resolution: Resolved: metadata privacy is surface-specific; canonical IDs stay above provider routing, private delivery uses scoped opaque capabilities/randomized outer envelopes, exposure is declared per role/path, and stronger padding/anonymity remains policy-selectable with honest limits.

question: Adversarially harden abuse controls without universal central control: blocking/reporting, delegated moderation, spam/admission, bans/timeouts, appeals/forks, malicious admins, illegal-content/operator exposure, service/bot abuse and portability of moderation state where appropriate.
provisional_direction: Keep enforcement scoped to users/Rooms/Spaces/providers and evidence explicit; no SeedLife universal moderator, global trust score or hidden master-ban authority.
resolution: Resolved: moderation/enforcement is user/Room/Space/provider scoped; selective EvidencePackages and optional signed SafetyAdvisories enable collaboration without a universal moderator/reputation score/master ban list; provider denial never rewrites protocol identity.

question: Run the 20-year anti-capture/continuity pass: SeedLife/forge/CDN/provider disappearance, crypto primitive failure, dominant extensions/clients, protocol-generation coexistence, registry continuity, migration/fork rules and embrace-extend-extinguish resistance.
provisional_direction: Every critical dependency and governance surface needs a credible replacement/fork/migration path that preserves user identity/data where cryptographically possible and gives dominant implementations no special protocol rights.
resolution: Resolved: published generations are self-contained/mirrorable via Protocol Continuity Bundles, registry meanings are immutable, generations/forks coexist explicitly, provider/project/crypto failure has migration or honest re-verification paths, and dominant clients/extensions gain no protocol authority from market share.

question: How does a non-technical user get a working Home without creating a cloud account, and how is single-vendor monoculture prevented?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0102: Home tiers T0..T4, sponsored starter mailbox default from invites, second non-cloud reference provider (V-020, PR-013).

question: Which coercive/proximate adversaries and OS/browser leakage channels must the architecture address, and what does OM refuse to promise?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0103: non-silent device linking, lock/quick-lock/travel posture, per-platform leakage controls (V-021); no hidden-volume deniability promise.

question: How are vulnerabilities disclosed and remediated across independent implementations without a kill switch or central authority?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0104: classified disclosure, signed SecurityAdvisories as inputs, peer-local floors (PR-012).

question: How is an account closed, deleted, moved or memorialized without an operator?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0105: terminal AccountRetirement; minimal LegacyPolicy; V-002 extended.

question: How do defaults avoid silent identity loss/lockout for one- and two-device users while keeping recovery off by default?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0106: ContinuityAssessment and informed-off recovery.

question: How is the v1 classical-MLS group gap stated honestly and closed without inventing crypto?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0107: per-type PQ status, ReInit path, objective adoption triggers (V-019).

question: How can engineering be unlocked when some gates need implementations, without weakening gates?
provisional_direction: Found in the 2026-09-24 hardening review (HARDENING_REVIEW_20260924.md).
resolution: Resolved: ADR-0108/0109: two-phase gates, scoped unlock, independence, traceability, threat register.

question: SPQR/Triple Ratchet dependency: the only SPQR implementation (Signal spqr) is AGPL-3.0-only while om-core is MPL-2.0. Relicence/exception, clean-room implementation from the published spec, or licence change?
provisional_direction: ADR-0118 §2: (a) and (b) in parallel; OM specifies its own SCKA wire/state format either way.
resolution: ADR-0118 (accepted 2026-09-24): option (d) — OM-Crypto-v1 is PQXDH + Double Ratchet without SPQR; clean-room SPQR/ML-KEM Braid from Signal's published specs is the planned OM-Crypto-v2 path. Relicensing ruled out.

question: How is the PQXDH X25519 identity key (used for DH and XEdDSA) bound to OM's DeviceIdentity (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65)? Should ML-DSA also sign PQ prekeys against quantum-server substitution (PQXDH §4.8)?
provisional_direction: DeviceIdentity dual-signs a certificate over the PQXDH IK within AccountControlState-authorised material; ML-DSA prekey signing needs a research ADR.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0131 rule 1: PQXDH identity and redirecting prekey material are bound to DeviceIdentity/ACS and require both Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 signatures.

question: Replays of last-resort (no one-time key) PQXDH handshakes: specify the replay cache (key, size, eviction, persistence, behavior after backup restore).
provisional_direction: Device-local cache keyed by SHA-256(tag||EK_A||CT), as in the V-001 prototype; interaction with ONE_TO_ONE_SESSION_MANAGEMENT §7 restore.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0131 rule 2: exact durable per-signed-prekey replay ledger keyed by transcript handshake_id, no probabilistic/LRU eviction, hard 4096 last-resort cap, fresh DeviceID/material after restore.

question: Pin the 1:1 AEAD and nonce-derivation rule in the OM-Crypto-v1 profile (the 2026-09-23 resolution says only 'misuse-resistant').
provisional_direction: AES-256-GCM-SIV (prototype) unless review prefers otherwise; ADR on the profile.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0131 rule 3: AES-256-GCM-SIV; HKDF-SHA256 derives disjoint 256-bit AEAD key and deterministic 96-bit nonce bound to authenticated header hash.

question: Ratchet headers (DH public key, counters, SCKA chunk) are plaintext to relays; is Double Ratchet header encryption required, given spqr has no header-encryption mode?
provisional_direction: Decide with V-015; the relay descriptor must state it.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0131 rule 4: no Double Ratchet header encryption in OM-Crypto-v1; exposure is explicit in metadata descriptors and measured by V-015; later profile may add it.

question: 'Post-quantum protection: on' wording: SPQR epochs took ~80 messages in the prototype, so PQ post-compromise healing is slow in quiet chats. UI and docs must promise handshake/HNDL protection plus eventual PQ healing, not per-message PQ healing.
provisional_direction: Amend ADR-0107 wording and SECURITY_PRIVACY_PROFILES.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0131 rule 5: UI promises post-quantum handshake/HNDL protection only; no v1 post-compromise PQ-healing or per-message PQ claim.

question: LegacyPolicy authorization (deferred from W0 by ADR-0127): where is the LegacyPolicy committed (guardian keys, threshold, minimum contest window), how do verifiers enforce the committed minimum window and the owner-inactivity precondition, and what are the wire semantics of the non-terminal LegacyRetirementPending state?
provisional_direction: Commit via a key-23 AccountControlState extension (W0 objects carry it unchanged, ADR-0113); reject windows below the committed minimum; model with AccountControl.tla ActivateLegacy. Must resolve before any release enables legacy_policy authorization.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0138 rule 1 as amended by ADR-0141: critical om.acs.legacy_policy commitment; unsupported verifiers reject the containing ACS; signed AccountRetirement is the wire claim; verifier-local inactivity then LegacyRetirementPending contest; guardian threshold is terminally narrow; eligible controllers including narrow quarantined challenge may veto. W0 still rejects legacy_policy retirement authorization and activation remains later-wave/off by default.

question: Unlinkable ACS binding for provider-stored AsyncKeyBundles: acs_generation/acs_state_hash are identical across an account's devices and providers; can the binding be verifiable by an authorized fetcher but uncorrelatable by the provider?
provisional_direction: W0 ships with the linkage disclosed in the metadata descriptor (device_count/stable_account_id: sometimes). Candidate: move the binding inside a per-relationship-encrypted field in a later AsyncKeyBundle object_version. Record the choice in V-015.
resolution: Resolved initially by ADR-0138 and strengthened/superseded by ADR-0140 before release: AsyncKeyBundle v1 itself omits clear account-wide ACS fields, fetchers validate against relationship-pinned trusted peer ACS, signed-prekey generation has a durable cross-provider recipient floor/equivocation hash, and one-time prekeys are context-bound; subject_device_id remains a disclosed stable per-device correlator.

question: Referral token profile: which Privacy Pass issuance protocol (RFC 9576-9578) and token type does a recipient use to issue referral tokens to contacts, how are tokens bound to the IntroGate, rate-limited and revoked, and how are they carried in IntroductionTicket/MessageRequest admission_proof?
provisional_direction: Recipient client as issuer, IntroGate as verifier (privately verifiable tokens), carried opaquely in admission_proof; covered by the V-016 IntroGate model.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0132 rule 1: RFC 9578 token type 0x0002 publicly verifiable Blind RSA, recipient-controlled issuer epoch, IntroGate public-key verification, one-time redemption, epoch rotation revocation.

question: Group call keys from a participant-set-bound MLS exporter can still be computed by any Room endpoint holding the epoch (non-joined members, full-room services, bridges), so an untrusted SFU could feed a silent listener. Which isolation mechanism makes 'a non-joined member cannot decrypt' true?
provisional_direction: Evaluate an RFC 9420 subgroup branch holding only joined participant devices (standard, rekeys on every join/leave) against per-sender SFrame keys sent only to joined participants; decide with V-007 before the calls scope unlocks (ADR-0128 rule 14).
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0132 rule 2: Room MLS authenticates call control only; per-sender SFrame keys are distributed over authenticated pairwise device channels only to joined participant DeviceIDs and rekey on membership generation change.

question: Should OM ever offer deniable group authentication (e.g. MLS credentials that do not chain durably to AccountID)?
provisional_direction: Not a v1 goal; would need a research ADR under absolute rule 3. v1 documents transferable group sender authentication (ADR-0128 rule 3, T-060).
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0138 rule 3: cryptographic group deniability is not an OM v1 property; MLS Rooms are transferably authenticated. Any deniable-group mode requires a separate future research CryptoProfile and cannot weaken ordinary MLS semantics.

question: Normative Home API: operations for relay deposit/drain/ack/rotate, per-contact deposit-capability mint/revoke, IntroGate, descriptor publishing, sponsorship redemption, RecoveryRecord store and fan-out, blob spool and BlobLocationRecord repair, forwarding 'moved'; request authentication; CDDL request/response bodies; a typed error registry (quota, moved, retryable, ...); versioning. Also a real ProviderCapabilities JSON Schema with durability_class, sketches for KeyMaterialProvider, BackupStore, RecoveryStore, StoragePool and CryptoProvider, and NetworkTransport.
provisional_direction: Write spec/protocol/home-api (CDDL + error registry) from PROVIDER_CONFORMANCE_SUITE cases; freeze it under V-020 before provider_reference; the conformance runner targets it (ADR-0130 rule 11).
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0133 rule 1 and spec/protocol/home-api.md + spec/cddl/home-api.cddl + om-home-errors registry; ProviderCapabilities is a real JSON Schema and missing interfaces are specified.

question: Release-transparency log protocol for OM releases: which append-only log design (for example a Sigstore/Rekor-style or CT-style log with signed checkpoints), how monitors publish signed observations, how clients and ClientHost controllers fetch two independent observations, and privacy of those fetches.
provisional_direction: Pick an existing reviewed log design; no novel log. Roles and failure behavior are fixed in SOFTWARE_SUPPLY_CHAIN §6 (ADR-0130 rule 5); record the choice with V-023.
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0133 rule 2: Rekor-v2/C2SP-checkpoint compatible transparency log with signed inclusion/consistency evidence and two independent monitor observations; privacy-preserving batch snapshot retrieval; log is evidence, not update authority.

question: Case lists for the planned W0 conformance suites registered in machine/conformance_suites.json (identity, discovery, attachments, security_floor, accessibility, identifier_spoofing, performance, ui_intents, ui_themes): each needs a specified case list like PROVIDER_CONFORMANCE_SUITE before its scope is authorized.
provisional_direction: Write one short case-list document per suite (or a section of the owning doc), then flip the suite's status to specified; the validator refuses scope authorization while a suite listing it is planned (ADR-0130 rule 10).
resolution: Resolved by ADR-0133 rule 3: all W0 suites now have concrete case lists in owning docs and are marked specified.

question: How can a recovery-alone activation delay be verified under request withholding or a late/offline verifier without trusting a Home clock?
provisional_direction: Use verifier-local first-observation time rather than a global trusted timestamp.
resolution: ADR-0131 rule 6: each verifier starts its own monotonic activation interval on first valid observation; a late verifier waits its own full delay; Homes/custodians cannot shorten it.

question: Can a stale rebasable reduction remove a later re-added/regranted incarnation of the same semantic principal (ABA)?
provisional_direction: Target immutable authority instances rather than semantic names.
resolution: ADR-0131 rule 7: every reducible object has an immutable incarnation id/creation digest; stale reduction is no-op when that exact instance is absent and never matches a later incarnation.

question: How does the accepting recipient authenticate the requester's intro identity to the requester's stable AccountID without exposing AccountID before acceptance?
provisional_direction: Symmetric post-acceptance IntroIdentityBinding.
resolution: ADR-0131 rule 8: both parties exchange and verify IntroIdentityBinding after acceptance; relationship is ACCEPTED_UNBOUND until both verify, then ACTIVE.

question: Which reviewed PQ/T HPKE KEM/profile defines MessageRequest encryption, since RFC 9180 alone does not define X25519+ML-KEM-768?
provisional_direction: Pin the current IETF HPKE PQ/T draft by version; never invent a hybrid KEM.
resolution: ADR-0131 rule 9: draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 MLKEM768-X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + ChaCha20Poly1305, base mode; incompatible later standard text requires a new profile/version.

question: Can OM enforce local plaintext-taint network restrictions after plaintext is delivered to a remote-origin mini-app?
provisional_direction: Treat disclosure to a remote origin as egress itself.
resolution: ADR-0132 rule 3: remote mini-app receives plaintext only through one-shot user disclosure or explicit conversation-authorized recipient/service path; host fetch denial is not claimed as containment.

question: Where is bilateral plaintext_egress policy for 1:1 conversations represented and revoked interoperably?
provisional_direction: Signed relationship policy consent from each participant; effective policy is intersection.
resolution: ADR-0132 rule 4: RelationshipPolicyConsent from each participant, monotone unilateral revoke, staleness fails closed.

question: Sealed-sender outer envelope for 1:1 delivery: every OM-Crypto-v1 envelope starts with the sender's EncodeEC(IK), a stable per-device correlator the recipient's mailbox Home sees and can link across the mailboxes it hosts. Can a later CryptoProfile hide the sender device key (and the DR header) from the relay layer?
provisional_direction: W0 ships with the exposure declared (stable_device_correlator: always on mailbox-class Homes, ADR-0136 rule 5). Candidate: an outer HPKE layer to the recipient device keyed per relationship, in a new CryptoProfile together with DR header encryption.
resolution: ADR-0142 supersedes the later-profile disposition: OM-Crypto-v1 established 1:1 mailbox/relay delivery wraps the complete ordinary envelope in SealedDeliveryEnvelope. Per-device/per-route signed delivery-key records remain relationship-private, first contact uses MessageRequest plus a request-scoped reply key, and clear-sender fallback is forbidden.
